transcript:
Meeting: Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo - ZenHealth
Date: 2025-03-18
Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Ivy Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (ZenHealth Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (ZenHealth VP Product), Sara Liu (ZenHealth Data Engineer)
Shared artifacts: Demo deck (https://redwood.app/decks/zenhealth-eval.pdf), Benchmark sheet (drive.google.com/zenhealth-benchmarks)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring features focusing on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Discussed how to integrate prompt sets into the Console, set up regression alerting tied to golden examples, and how Optimize suggests batching/quantization settings. Agreed to run a pilot with 50-100 prompts and automated regression checks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We have Marcus our SE and Ivy from CS. Priya, Carlos, Sara, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Thanks, yeah excited to see the eval stuff. We're trying to get a handle on drift and quality regressions post-deploy.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: Great. Quick agenda — i'll demo the Console eval flow, how you build prompt sets, run A/B comparisons, and then the regression alerting tied to golden labels. we'll also show some Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching.
[00:40] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. Our main constraints are latency under 300ms p50 for chat completions and no degradation in clinical extraction accuracy beyond 1.5% — otherwise product stakeholders will push back.
[00:55] Marcus Chen: Understood. We'll show how you can lock a baseline and create alerts for exact-match and custom metrics.
[01:10] Sara Liu: Quick Q — For the pilot, how do you want us to format the prompt set? CSV? JSONL?
[01:18] Marcus Chen: Either works; we prefer JSONL with fields for prompt, expected_answer, tolerance. We'll send a template. It's in the benchmark sheet we shared.
[01:30] Priya Raman: Also curious about private deployments — we can't send PHI outside the VPC for now. Is Redwood Optimize compatible with private?
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: Yes — Redwood Private supports the same Console features, you just point the control plane to your VPC. There may be extra steps for KMS integration for key management. We'll include the private deployment checklist in the security pack.
[01:55] Marcus Chen: Ok jumping into the Console — i'm screen sharing now. You'll see Eval > Prompt sets. Here we created a sample prompt set called zenhealth-pilot-50. It contains prompts, golden labels, and tags for reason codes.
[02:15] Marcus Chen: (typing) The UI lets you upload JSONL, map columns, and assign scoring metrics: BLEU, token overlap, exact match, or custom regex. For extraction tasks we recommend a combination of exact match and normalized F1.
[02:40] Priya Raman: And can we weight metrics? For example extraction precision matters more than recall for us.
[02:48] Marcus Chen: Yes, you can assign weights per metric and the overall score will be a weighted sum. We persist the baseline score when you pin a release.
[03:05] Carlos Mendez: How do A/B comparisons work? We need to compare two model variants and see where one degrades by example.
[03:14] Marcus Chen: Good question. In the A/B tab you select two runs — baseline and candidate — the system shows per-example diffs, bubbles for severity, and can export examples where the candidate is worse beyond a threshold. You can also surface toggles to triage by confidence or token-level differences.
[03:40] Sara Liu: Is the per-example diff available via API? We want to programmatically pull failing examples into our ticketing system.
[03:49] Marcus Chen: Yep — there's an eval API endpoint that returns per-prompt results with fields for baseline_output, candidate_output, metric_scores, and a diff tag. Note: api keys follow the same RBAC rules; if you're on Private we'll integrate with your SSO.
[04:10] Priya Raman: Can the regression alerts be tied to a specific route or model tag? We have different routes for clinical extraction vs triage.
[04:20] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. Alerts are scoped to model+route+promptset. You can create alert policies that trigger on aggregate score drops or on counts of failing examples. They integrate with PagerDuty, Slack, and email.
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: Real quick caveat — transcription may have moved some product names around, but the Alerts UI has severity and runbook links.
[04:45] Carlos Mendez: What about false positives? If we see a blip due to sampling variation, can we suppress alerts?
[04:52] Marcus Chen: Yes, you can set lookback windows, minimum failing count, and require consecutive failing runs before alerting. There's also a 'mute' with notes for temporary suppressions.
[05:10] Priya Raman: Show us a demo of a real regression.
[05:15] Marcus Chen: Sure — i'm loading a past run. Here the baseline F1 is 0.92, candidate dropped to 0.88. In the UI you can click 'View failing examples' and it shows the prompts, baseline vs candidate, and suggested tags like 'tokenization-edge' which is often due to quantization artifacts.
[05:40] Marcus Chen: (mis-transcript) you'll also see K V cash hits — that's our KV cache optimization showing repeated prefix hits. Sometimes the transcript says K V cash which is funny.
[05:50] Sara Liu: Haha, yes earlier transcript we saw 'K V cash' — noted.
[06:00] Marcus Chen: On the side panel is 'A/B analysis' which surfaces where the model is regressing by intent cluster. You can export these to CSV or push to your JIRA using our webhook.
[06:20] Priya Raman: For clinical extraction we need deterministic eval. Does Redwood support seeding or forcing deterministic outputs for eval runs?
[06:30] Marcus Chen: You can run evaluations in deterministic mode (temperature=0, fixed sampling) and the eval runner records all sampling params. For production monitoring we recommend running with the same sampling policy as prod, but the pilot can start deterministic to get a baseline.
[06:50] Carlos Mendez: About A/B: can we run multi-armed rollouts tied to quality metrics, not just traffic? For instance auto-fallback if candidate reduces entity extraction by >1%.
[07:05] Marcus Chen: We have rollout policies in Console. You can define a custom metric (the eval score) and define automated rollback when the metric drops beyond threshold. It's driven by the eval pipeline that ingests your prompt set and live samples.
[07:30] Lena Ortiz: Another thing — Redwood Optimize will analyze your workload and suggest quantization profiles and batching parameters to hit cost/latency targets. We'll show a sample Optimize run.
[07:45] Marcus Chen: Switching to Optimize tab. Here Optimize suggested switching a model to 4-bit quant and a specific kernel selection which reduced median latency by 18% and cost per token by 24% in our internal benchmark. It also has caveats — we surface expected quality delta and a confidence band.
[08:10] Priya Raman: How do you recommend we validate quality after quantization?
[08:15] Marcus Chen: Use the eval runner to re-run your prompt set on the quantized candidate and compare A/B. The system will flag any per-example regressions. We also recommend a small canary on traffic with shadow mode to compare live outputs without impacting users.
[08:35] Sara Liu: Shadow mode — is that supported in Private?
[08:40] Marcus Chen: Yes — you can run identical requests to both models inside your VPC; the control plane just records results. For air-gapped deployments there's an on-prem agent that runs the eval runner locally. We'll include more in the private checklist.
[08:58] Carlos Mendez: Security questions — are logs preserved? We need audit logs for model changes and eval runs.
[09:05] Lena Ortiz: We persist audit trails, and for Private you can forward logs to your SIEM. For hosted we offer configurable retention and a SOC 2 report. We'll share the security pack.
[09:20] Priya Raman: Can we store golden labels encrypted with our KMS?
[09:25] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for secrets and golden sets on Private deployments — again, part of the security docs.
[09:40] Carlos Mendez: Back to the eval UI — can you show metrics trending over time? We want regression alerts to show historical trend lines and sample counts.
[09:50] Marcus Chen: Yep — the dashboard shows a time-series for your primary metric with shaded confidence intervals and markers for releases. You can drill into any point and see the failing examples for that run.
[10:10] Priya Raman: For our compliance team, we'd like to store snapshots of prompt sets tied to release IDs. Is that automatic?
[10:18] Marcus Chen: When you pin a baseline we snapshot the prompt set, the model revision, and the scoring config. Snapshots are exportable as JSONL and haved a release tag.
[10:30] Lara — (transcription glitch)
[10:35] Carlos Mendez: You mentioned triage — is there built-in labeling to classify failure modes?
[10:40] Marcus Chen: Yes — in the triage workflow you can add labels like 'entity-missing', 'hallucination', 'tokenization-edge', 'prompt-format'. You can also set automation rules to tag certain regex matches.
[11:00] Priya Raman: Can we get per-customer segmentation? Our customer support needs to see failing prompts per account.
[11:08] Marcus Chen: You can attach metadata to each incoming request (account id, route, user id) and filter the eval results by metadata. For Private, that metadata stays inside your VPC.
[11:25] Sara Liu: Practical question: how much effort to run the pilot? What staffing do you need on our side?
[11:33] Lena Ortiz: For a 4-week pilot, typically we ask for 1-2 engineers (to prepare prompts and wiring) and 1 product stakeholder for acceptance. Redwood SE will run the initial eval and bench.
[11:45] Priya Raman: That should be fine. We'll allocate a SWE and a data eng.
[11:50] Marcus Chen: We'll also provide a pre-built ingestion script that maps your logs to prompt set records. It's in the benchmark sheet.
[12:05] Carlos Mendez: Any limitations with long context? We have documents with 3k-5k tokens.
[12:12] Marcus Chen: The runtime supports long context; the eval runner will score based on truncated windows or whole-doc matching depending on your metric. For cost reasons Optimize may suggest chunking and specialized kernels.
[12:30] Priya Raman: Regarding false positives again — if a metric dips temporarily because of upstream data change, can we attach annotations to runs so the alert isn't escalated?
[12:40] Marcus Chen: Yes — the run and alert pages support annotations and runbook links; you can also require manual ack for certain sev levels.
[12:55] Sara Liu: Will the pilot include perf benchmarks? We want to see p50/p95 numbers for our dataset.
[13:01] Marcus Chen: Yes — pilot includes a perf pass. We'll run the prompt set through our internal load harness and provide p50/p95 and token throughput. We'll include both hosted and a Dedicated estimate.
[13:20] Priya Raman: Pricing question — how is eval usage billed?
[13:25] Lena Ortiz: Eval runs are billed per-token similar to inference, but we offer pilot credits and a capped pilot cost. For Dedicated customers we include a baseline eval quota. We'll include pricing details in the follow-up.
[13:40] Carlos Mendez: About A/B exports — can we get a CSV that includes token-level diffs?
[13:47] Marcus Chen: Yep — export includes token diffs, scores, and a short reason code extraction.
[14:00] Priya Raman: Are there any known model compat issues? Like with certain LoRA or adapter formats?
[14:08] Marcus Chen: For finetuned models we support standard HF checkpoints and adapter formats; for some custom op kernels there can be limitations but we'll validate during model onboarding.
[14:25] Lena Ortiz: Quick demo note — transcripts sometimes mangle acronyms, apologies if you see V P C or K V cash.
[14:32] Priya Raman: Noted.
[14:35] Marcus Chen: Back to the UI — i'll create a new alert policy: Name 'Clinical extraction drop'. Scope: model: redwood-bert-clinic:v3, route: /extract, promptset: zenhealth-pilot-50. Trigger: overall score drop > 1% and failing count > 10 in 24h window. Notification: Slack #ml-alerts, PagerDuty.
[14:58] Marcus Chen: (typing) Also adding a mute window for scheduled maintenance.
[15:10] Carlos Mendez: Good. Can the system auto-attach examples to the Slack alert?
[15:16] Marcus Chen: It posts a summary and a link — you can configure to attach top N failing examples inline, but we usually link to the Console to avoid PII in Slack.
[15:30] Priya Raman: For our compliance team, links must be behind SSO. Does Redwood support SAML?
[15:36] Lena Ortiz: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. We'll include the SSO setup doc.
[15:50] Sara Liu: One more on Optimize — does it recommend batching sizes per route? Our routes have very different payload sizes.
[15:58] Marcus Chen: It analyzes request distribution and suggests batching and micro-batching strategies per route, along with suggested maximum tokens per batch. You can apply per-route overrides.
[16:15] Priya Raman: Any gotchas when applying Optimize recommendations?
[16:20] Marcus Chen: The main tradeoff is quality vs cost — some quant profiles can introduce small regressions. Optimize surfaces an expected quality delta and confidence band so you can decide to canary it.
[16:35] Carlos Mendez: Ok let's talk timeline. We want a pilot run for 3-4 weeks and then an internal review.
[16:43] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Proposed timeline: you send prompts by 3/22, we kick off initial eval by 3/25, perf run by 3/27, and a mid-pilot review week of 4/7.
[16:58] Priya Raman: Works for us.
[17:05] Marcus Chen: Final quick note on A/B: the UI supports tagging examples as 'do not include in metric' if a prompt is deemed irreproducible; this helps reduce noise.
[17:18] Sara Liu: Good to know.
[17:25] Lena Ortiz: Okay wrapping up — we'll send the security pack, benchmark template, and pilot agreement. Any final questions?
[17:32] Priya Raman: No, that's it for now. Thanks everyone.
[17:36] Carlos Mendez: Thanks.
[17:40] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all — we'll follow up with next steps and calendar invites.

Recap & Next Steps:
- Redwood to send SOC2/security pack and SSO docs (Lena)
- SE to share benchmarking spreadsheet + ingestion script (Marcus)
- ZenHealth to provide prompt set (50-100) and golden labels (Sara/Priya)
- Schedule pilot kickoff 2025-03-25

End of recording.
